title: Cloud Migration: AWS Native vs Multi-Cloud Kubernetes
primaryRecommendation: AWS Native Managed Services (ECS/EKS with Aurora)
recommendationRationale: AWS Native achieves 38% faster time-to-market, $420k lower initial setup cost, and eliminates specialized Kubernetes cluster reliability engineering overhead while staying within manageable lock-in thresholds.
author: Marcus Vance (VP of Platform Engineering)

scenario.problem: Legacy monolithic infrastructure reaching end-of-life; annual maintenance costs surging by 40% with recurring downtime during traffic spikes.

options.name: Option A: AWS Native Managed Stack
options.summary: Full adoption of AWS Serverless and Managed Containers (ECS/Fargate, Aurora Serverless v2, DynamoDB).
cons: Egress cost uncertainty at extreme volume

options.name: Option B: Multi-Cloud Kubernetes (EKS + GKE)
options.summary: Platform-agnostic Helm/Terraform architecture deployable identically across AWS and GCP to eliminate lock-in.
cons: Higher network complexity and cross-cloud latency

options.name: Option C: Hybrid Private Colocation + Cloud Bursting
options.summary: Keep core databases on existing leased bare-metal hardware and burst stateless services to public cloud.
pros: Predictable compute billing for steady-state workloads

finRisk.insights: Option A achieves an estimated ROI of 240% over 3 years. Payback period is 7.2 months versus 19.4 months for Option B.

opsVelocity.insights: Option A reduces deployment lead time from 14 days to under 30 minutes. SRE toil reduced by 65%.

stratAlign.verdict: Favors Option A, with Option B noted for vendor neutrality
stratAlign.insights: Time-to-market advantage in Option A enables capturing early market demand 4 months before competitors.

governance.verdict: Conditional approval for Option A with data escrow strategy
governance.insights: AWS Native passes SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliance checks out-of-the-box.

title: AI Infrastructure: On-Premise GPU Cluster vs Serverless Hyperscaler
primaryRecommendation: Hybrid Cloud Bursting (Core Reserved Cloud GPUs + On-Demand)
recommendationRationale: Pure on-premise hardware risks immediate obsolescence given rapid 9-month GPU hardware generation cycles, while purely on-demand cloud is 3.1x more expensive. Reserved cloud instances with intelligent queue bursting delivers the optimal cost-to-flexibility ratio.
author: Dr. Sarah Chen (Chief AI Scientist)

scenario.problem: Foundation model fine-tuning and inference bills climbing to $180k/month; engineering team facing compute shortages during training runs.

options.name: Option A: Hybrid Cloud GPU Clusters (Reserved + Spot)
options.summary: 1-year reserved instances on Lambda Cloud / RunPod + automated fallback to AWS H100s for spike workloads.
cons: Network latency for ultra-massive cluster interconnect (InfiniBand)
Long-term commitment risk on specific GPU architectures

options.name: Option B: Dedicated On-Premises DGX Cluster (CapEx)
options.summary: Procure 8x NVIDIA H200 server nodes housed in a tier-4 colocation facility.
pros: Lowest marginal cost per GPU hour at 100% utilization
cons: Requires high-voltage power & liquid cooling contracts

finRisk.insights: Option A preserves liquid capital and avoids $1.8M CapEx depreciation risk during rapid AI hardware shifts.

opsVelocity.insights: Option A delivers GPUs immediately; Option B risks 5 months of halted research pipeline waiting on shipments.

stratAlign.insights: Enables agility to pivot to new inference architectures (e.g. mixture-of-agents, specialized FP8 chips) without hardware lock-in.

governance.verdict: Conditional approval with Private VPC Peering
governance.insights: Direct VPC connection ensures customer training datasets never traverse public routing networks.

tradeoffComparison.criterion: Lead Time to Training First Model
